findings.why_this_severity: Q7 (a human-facing artifact, the skill's own shipped result.json) would place this at major, but Q9 drops it a step — the miss is already visible in the shipped record itself, so any maintainer opening evals/result.json sees the exact failing rows and can route around them or re-narrow the description without losing anything — and Q10 drops it a further step since I read the shipped result rather than re-running fresh probes myself (only n=2 per query, which meta:skill-eval's own text flags as too small to trust on its own).
findings.where: plugins/no-code-prose/skills/policy/evals/result.json (trigger.results) and the boundary clause in plugins/no-code-prose/skills/policy/SKILL.md's description frontmatter
findings.problem: The skill's own shipped measurement shows its stated boundary failing in practice: the description explicitly says 'Do NOT use for writing the document itself... an ADR... is written by the skill that owns that document, not this one,' yet the recorded eval shows the should-NOT-trigger ADR query firing 2 of 2 runs (pass: false), and a should-trigger query ('leave a deprecation note in the code...') missing 0 of 2 (pass: false) — both shipped without narrowing the description or recording the gap as an accepted exception, contrary to meta:skill-eval's own house rule that 'a should-NOT-trigger query that fires IS a real failure... not a rounding error.'
findings.scenario: A user asks 'Write the ADR for our decision to match ledger entries by external reference instead of row id.' With no-code-prose:policy installed, the skill's own recorded measurement shows it fires anyway (2/2 runs), pulling the session toward the comment-form rule instead of leaving ADR authorship alone — precisely the case its own description carves out as not its ground.
findings.evidence: plugins/no-code-prose/skills/policy/evals/result.json rows for query 'Write the ADR for our decision...' (should_trigger: false, triggers: 2, runs: 2, pass: false) and 'Leave a note in the code that this endpoint is deprecated...' (should_trigger: true, triggers: 0, runs: 2, pass: false); meta:skill-eval SKILL.md, section 'Reading the result': 'A should-NOT-trigger query that fires IS a real failure: the description is too broad, narrow it.'
